newsitem.title: USA: British ADRs mixed in wake of Labour victory.
newsitem.headline: British ADRs mixed in wake of Labour victory.

text.p: American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) of British companies were mixed on Friday in the wake of Labour's overwhelming election victory, traders and analysts said.
They said ADRs in companies that rely on exports or have a significant presence overseas were boosted by a slump in sterling after Tony Blair's Labour Party trounced the long-ruling Conservatives.
However, power companies were off amid expectations Labour would impose a one-time multibillion-pound windfall tax on privatized utilities.
"The basic message is that U.K. equities took the overall victory fairly well, but basically sterling took a hit," said Andrew Melinek, head of ADR research and sales at NatWest Securities.
He said British ADRs could see a period of uncertainty until Labour presents its budget.
Val Kosmider, head of international equity trading at Schroder Wertheim, said the British currency had been weighed by the transition of power.
"For the most part, they are doing what you'd expect them to be doing," he said of British ADRs.
"The shares that would tend to (do) poorly are the utilities, which are down, and international stocks are holding on ... because the pound is quite weak."
Among multinational ADRs, British Steel Plc rose one to 23-3/4 on heavy volume. The company was among the most active ADRs in New York.
Reuters Holdings Plc, a news and information company, rose 1-5/16 to 66. Hanson Plc was up 5/8 to 25-1/8.
Among utility stocks, PowerGen Plc fell two to 40-7/8, and National Power Plc was off 1/2 to 33. British Telecommunications Plc fell 1/8 to 74.
